newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - Australian copper output seen rising in 96/97.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - Australian copper output seen rising in 96/97.

text.p: Australian copper output will rise in the year to June 30, 1997 to 490,000 tonnes of refined production from 300,000 tonnes in 1995/96, the Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics (ABARE) said.

The bureau, the Australian government's main commodity forecasting agency, said Australian export earnings would rise as higher export volume offset lower prices and the effect of a stronger Australian dollar.
Export earnings would be 16 percent higher at A$928 million in 1995/96 and would rise a further 10 percent to A$1,018 million in 1996/97, ABARE said in its September quarter Commodities bulletin.

In 1996/97, Australian unrefined mine production would rise by a further nine percent to 490,000 tonnes, with output at existing operations maintained and output at new facilities expanding towards capacity, ABARE said.
Australian copper mine production recovered by 28 percent in 1995/96 to reach 448,000 tonnes, after a fall of nearly 19 percent in 1994/95, it said.
"Mount Isa contributed to the turnaround, with production returning to more normal levels following the resolution of a major industrial dispute," it said.
The enterprise bargaining agreements struck by staff was expected to help sustain the higher levels of output from the mine.
